name: Earth
label: Southern Lord
lede: Dylan Carlson took heavy metal riffs, slowed them to a crawl and made a 73-minute record with no drums. Then he vanished for years and came back playing western noir.

eras.title: Named after Black Sabbath's old band
eras.text: Dylan Carlson starts Earth in Olympia with one idea: play metal riffs at a crawl and hold them for as long as it takes. The early records are cheap, loud and in no hurry to be catchy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Earth (American band) · Red Bull Music Academy
years.h: Dylan Carlson names Earth after Black Sabbath's old band
years.p: Carlson forms the band in Olympia with Slim Moon and Greg Babior. He lists La Monte Young, King Crimson and Slayer as influences.
years.xp:
Earth borrows the name Black Sabbath used before they were Black Sabbath. Moon went on to found Kill Rock Stars.

Carlson boiled the plan down in a 2017 lecture: "What if we take a Slayer-style riff and play it for 20 minutes at half speed? That was my one good idea." He found Young's work through the Velvet Underground and the minimalist composers, and added oblique motion: a fixed drone with other notes moving against it.

years.h: A $300 session at Smegma Studios
years.p: Earth's first recording session happens in Portland on a shoestring, Carlson says. It becomes the raw material for the band's earliest releases.

years.cap: Dylan Carlson with Kathleen Hanna, Bruce Pavitt and Krist Novoselic, Paramount Theater, Seattle, October 31, 1991
years.h: Extra-Capsular Extraction puts Earth on Sub Pop
years.p: The debut EP is feedback and low-end riffing. [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]], a friend of Carlson's, contributed vocals, according to The Quietus.
years.xp: Seattle Weekly has Cobain screaming on it. The Quietus puts it more mildly: he contributed some vocals. Either way, Cobain was a friend of both Earth and the Melvins.

eras.title: The void at the heart of grunge
eras.text: Seattle is busy selling flannel when Carlson records an album with no drums and no vocals. Earth 2 becomes the blueprint for drone metal. The band itself slowly comes apart.

years.h: Earth tracks three songs at Avast! in Seattle
years.p: Carlson and bassist Dave Harwell work with producer Stuart Hallerman; Joe Burns adds percussion on one track only. The Quietus calls the sound "a slow-motion pyroclastic flow of guitars."
years.xp: Carlson has said he regrets not recording at the band's full live volume. The sessions yield the three tracks that become Earth 2.

years.big: "What if we take a Slayer-style riff and play it for 20 minutes at half speed?"
q: Very claustrophobic, but I'm very glad people responded to it.
years.src: Wikipedia: Earth 2 · The Quietus · Red Bull Music Academy
years.h: Sub Pop releases a record with no drums and no vocals
years.p: Carlson's own summary of Earth 2, from his 2017 lecture. Its three tracks run 15, 27 and 30 minutes, and AllMusic's John Bush wrote that it "virtually created" drone and ambient metal.
years.xp:
The tracks are Seven Angels, Teeth of Lions Rule the Divine and Like Gold and Faceted, 73 minutes and a second in all. Guitar World's Jonathan Horsley called it "a massage chair for the inner ear."

Stephen O'Malley later named a group Teeth of Lions Rule the Divine after the second track, and The Quietus says Sunn O))) owe the record a debt nearly impossible to repay.

years.h: Sunn Amps and Smashed Guitars catches the live noise
years.p: The live recordings from this period land on Sunn Amps and Smashed Guitars. A later reissue adds a demo, Divine and Bright, with Cobain singing lead.

years.src: Wikipedia: Earth (American band) · Wikipedia: Dylan Carlson
years.h: Carlson buys the shotgun Cobain asked for
years.p: On March 30 Cobain asks his friend Dylan Carlson to buy a shotgun, saying it's for protection. Cobain dies by suicide on April 5, and Carlson later ties his heroin addiction to that period.
years.xp: Carlson has said his heroin dependency intensified after Cobain's death. He now lives in recovery, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Phase 3: Thrones and Dominions lands as the lineup churns
years.p: Earth's third record arrives amid constant personnel changes and the start of Carlson's decline.

years.h: Pentastar adds vocals and a rock swing, then Earth goes quiet
years.p: The last record before the break brings in singing and a riffier feel. No full-length studio album follows until 2005.

eras.title: Heroin, a missing guitar, then Hex
eras.text: Carlson spends years lost to addiction, rehab and legal trouble, and by his own account doesn't own a guitar. He comes back with slow country grooves and a drummer who stays.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dylan Carlson · Red Bull Music Academy
years.h: Carlson rebuilds Earth around Adrienne Davies
years.p: Drummer Davies is the first time live drums are a fixture in Earth. The band keeps the slowness and drops the wall of noise.
years.xp:
Carlson blames legal and drug problems for the gap between albums. He lived in Los Angeles for about four years, didn't play guitar, and started again around 2001 or 2002, per Wikipedia.

Davies became his musical partner for the rest of the band's run. They were married and later separated, and she remains in Earth.

years.h: WNYC puts Earth back on the air
years.p: Earth plays a live session at the New York station, an early sign that Carlson is performing again.

years.h: KK Null joins Earth on a European tour
years.p: The Japanese noise guitarist tours with Carlson and Davies, who also record the Dexamyl material.

years.src: Wikipedia: Earth (American band) · Red Bull Music Academy · The Obelisk
years.h: Earth trades distortion for twang on Hex
years.p: With Davies on drums, the band reaches for Duane Eddy, Merle Haggard and Ennio Morricone. It's the first "new Earth" record, and the first on Southern Lord.
years.xp:
Carlson met [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]], who runs Southern Lord and plays in [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]], around 2003; he's told the story as a meeting at a Goat Snake show. Carlson has said Sunn O))) took its name from the amps.

Hex set the template: long, spare western-noir instrumentals where a single riff gets stretched and shaded.
play: Hex: Or Printing in the Infernal Method

eras.title: Bill Frisell and the lion's skull
eras.text: Southern Lord becomes home. Earth grows into a proper band, adds keys, upright bass and a jazz guitarist, and makes a record critics treat as a leap.

years.h: Hibernaculum re-records old Earth songs in the Hex mold
years.p: Only A Plague of Angels is new, at over 16 minutes. A DVD documentary by Seldon Hunt, Within the Drone, ships with it.
years.xp: Randall Dunn produced at Aleph Studios. Don McGreevy plays bass, Steve Moore trombone and organ, and Anderson a Korg MS-20. The band considers it an EP at about 37 minutes. Pitchfork gave it 7.8.

years.h: Bill Frisell sits in on The Bees Made Honey in the Lion's Skull
years.p: The jazz guitarist plays on three tracks. Randall Dunn produces, with Steve Moore on piano and Hammond organ and Don McGreevy on bass.
years.xp:
Critics liked it: The Quietus gave it 9/10, Pitchfork 7.7 and The A.V. Club an A. The record pulls in late-1960s San Francisco bands, jazz and film music.

The title points to Samson and the lion in Judges 14, and several song titles come from Cormac McCarthy's Blood Meridian.

eras.title: Cello, British folk, then a rock record
eras.text: Earth leans toward British folk-rock and adds Lori Goldston's cello for two Angels albums. Then it tightens into something close to a rock band, with guest singers.

years.src: Wikipedia: Angels of Darkness, Demons of Light I · Wikipedia: Dylan Carlson
years.h: Angels of Darkness, Demons of Light I brings in a cello
years.p: Lori Goldston joins on cello and Karl Blau plays bass, with Pentangle and Fairport Convention in the air. Carlson called it more melodic and riff-oriented.
years.xp: It was recorded in April 2010, while Carlson was recovering from hepatitis B and liver failure, per Wikipedia. Metacritic scored it 82, and the five tracks run 60 minutes, 20 of them on the title track.

years.cap: Dylan Carlson live with Earth, April 2012
years.h: Angels II was already recorded when Part I came out
years.p: The sequel leans harder on improvisation.

years.cap: Earth live at Fever, Tokyo, June 6, 2014
years.h: Primitive and Deadly lets Earth be a rock band
years.p: Mark Lanegan sings on two tracks and Rabia Shaheen Qazi on one, the first vocals on an Earth record since 1996.
years.xp: Recorded at Rancho de la Luna in Joshua Tree and at Avast in Seattle with Randall Dunn. Bill Herzog plays bass, with guitarists Brett Netson and Jodie Cox. The band said it let itself be a rock band and approached traditional pop structures. Metacritic gave it 80.

eras.title: Desert concrete, a new label
eras.text: Earth teams up with dub producer The Bug, moves to Sargent House and keeps grinding.

years.h: Concrete Desert pairs Earth with Kevin Martin's The Bug
years.p: The dub producer and Earth release a collaborative album.

years.cap: Dylan Carlson live at Hafenklang, Hamburg
years.src: Wikipedia: Full Upon Her Burning Lips
years.h: Full Upon Her Burning Lips moves Earth to Sargent House
years.p: The ninth studio album runs ten tracks and 62 minutes, with a US tour that has Helms Alee opening.
years.xp: The lead single was Cats on the Briar, out March 6, 2019. The tour ran from May 24 to June 29. Metacritic averaged 79 across 12 reviews.

years.h: Earth pulls a Bologna show over a Palestinian flag
years.p: At the TPO social centre, the band cancels just before playing, objecting to the flag. Per Wikipedia the venue lost about 5,000 euros and started a crowdfunding campaign.
